Comment: Kali quantum task pipeline (account 060274391988): validate a circuit against a local/Braket simulator, pause for an explicit human approval (SNS + waitForTaskToken), then submit to a real Braket QPU only once approved. Must be deployed in a Braket-supported region (us-east-1, us-west-1, us-west-2, or eu-west-2) - the aws-sdk:braket:createQuantumTask integration always calls Braket in this state machine's own execution region, and Braket isn't offered in every AWS region (us-east-2 notably isn't). See aws/setup-kali-quantum-infra.sh, which fills in the __*__ placeholders below at deploy time - there is no free/local equivalent for Stage 3: a real quantum device task costs real money the moment it runs.

ValidateCircuit.Comment: Runs the circuit against a local/Braket simulator first - the SAME kind of validation Kali's existing run_quantum_circuit chat tool already does (see app/api/ai-one-chat/route.ts and quantum-service/main.py), just invoked as a state machine step instead of a chat tool call. kali-quantum-service.onrender.com is a plain third-party HTTPS endpoint (Render-hosted FastAPI, not AWS API Gateway) - that's why this uses the http:invoke SDK integration with an EventBridge Connection for its X-API-Key auth, not apigateway:invoke, which only works for actual API Gateway resources. quantum_braket.py returns qubit_count, estimated_cost_usd, circuit_summary, and circuit_action in its response body - CheckValidationStatus and RequestApproval below read those back out from $.validation.ResponseBody.

CheckValidationStatus.Comment: http:invoke reports a successful HTTP call (200) even when quantum_braket.py's own response body says {status: 'error'} (invalid circuit_code, exec() failure, etc.) - the Catch above only ever sees transport-level failures, not this. Without this explicit check, an invalid circuit would sail straight through to a human approver with missing qubit_count/estimated_cost_usd/circuit_summary fields instead of failing here for free.

ValidationFailed.Cause: The circuit failed local-simulator validation before ever reaching the approval/QPU stages - no cost was incurred.

RequestApproval.Comment: Pauses here until POST /api/kali/approve-task calls SendTaskSuccess or SendTaskFailure against $$.Task.Token - that route is the only thing that can move this forward. TimeoutSeconds below (24h) is a starting point, not a fixed requirement - tune it to how quickly you expect a human to actually respond. ResponseBody/snake_case field names below match quantum_braket.py's actual response shape and the http:invoke SDK integration's result wrapper - verify these against a real execution's history, since exact http:invoke result nesting wasn't confirmed against a live run before this was written.

Message.default.$: States.Format('Kali quantum task pending approval: {} qubits, target {}, est. ${}. Approve or reject via the dashboard.', $.validation.ResponseBody.qubit_count, $.target_qpu, $.validation.ResponseBody.estimated_cost_usd)

ApprovalTimedOut.Cause: No approval decision arrived within the timeout window - no QPU task was ever submitted, no cost was incurred.

ApprovalRejected.Cause: An approver explicitly rejected this task via POST /api/kali/approve-task - no QPU task was ever submitted, no cost was incurred.

ExecuteOnQpu.Comment: The only state in this whole machine that spends real money - everything above it exists specifically to gate this one call behind an explicit human decision. Action.$ now pulls circuit_action from the ValidateCircuit response itself (the OpenQASM IR of the SAME circuit a human just approved), not a separate top-level input field - submitting anything else here would mean the approver never actually saw what gets run. REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_BRAKET_RESULTS_BUCKET below with a real S3 bucket you own in this account/region.
